question: Find the missing number: 2, 12, 36, 80, 150, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 252.

GIVEN

• Series: 2, 12, 36, 80, 150, ?

SOLUTION

• Find the first differences: 12 − 2 = 10, 36 − 12 = 24, 80 − 36 = 44, 150 − 80 = 70.

• Second differences: 24 − 10 = 14, 44 − 24 = 20, 70 − 44 = 26 (rising by 6 each time).

• Third differences are constant (6, 6), so the next second difference = 26 + 6 = 32.

• Next first difference = 70 + 32 = 102, so the missing term = 150 + 102 = 252.

• Cross-check with a formula: the terms are n²(n + 1): 1²×2 = 2, 2²×3 = 12, 3²×4 = 36, 4²×5 = 80, 5²×6 = 150, so 6²×7 = 36 × 7 = 252.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Spot the pattern 1×2, 4×3, 9×4, 16×5, 25×6 (square × next number), so the next is 36×7 = 252.

NOTE

• Option 1 (245) is 7 × 35; it does not fit the constant third difference of 6 or the n²(n + 1) rule (it would need a last gap of 95).

• Option 3 (300) would need a last gap of 150, which breaks the second-difference pattern (14, 20, 26, 32).

• Option 4 (350) would need a last gap of 200, again far off the pattern.

• Useful for SSC and Railway exams: when differences are not constant, take differences of differences. If that fails, test n²(n ± 1), n³ ± n, and (n² + n) forms.

question:
From the given alternative words, select the word which can be formed using the letters of the given word.

QUINTESSENCE
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. QUITE.

GIVEN

• Given word: QUINTESSENCE = Q, U, I, N, T, E, S, S, E, N, C, E (12 letters: E×3, N×2, S×2, and Q, U, I, T, C once each).

SOLUTION

• Check each option letter by letter against the given word.

• SCOT: needs O, which is not in QUINTESSENCE. ✗

• QUOTE: needs O. ✗

• QUITE: Q, U, I, T, E are all present with the required counts. ✓

• ESTEEM: needs M, which is not in QUINTESSENCE (it also needs E three times, which is fine, but M is missing). ✗

• So the word that can be formed is QUITE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• First scan for a letter that is absent from the given word. O and M are absent, so SCOT, QUOTE and ESTEEM are eliminated at once.

NOTE

• Option 1 (SCOT) and Option 2 (QUOTE) fail because the letter O is not available.

• Option 4 (ESTEEM) fails because the letter M is not available.

• In "word formation" questions, always check both the letters and their frequency (a letter cannot be used more times than it appears).

question:
Read the two given statements carefully, followed by conclusions I and II. Determine which of the conclusions logically follow from the statements, ignoring any commonly known facts or real-world knowledge.

Statements:

All bed are wood.

Some chair are bed.

Conclusion:

I. Some woods are chair.

II. Some woods are bed.
option_2: Both conclusion I and II follows
option_4: Either conclusion I or II follows
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Both conclusion I and II follows.

GIVEN

• Statement 1: All bed are wood (A-type).

• Statement 2: Some chair are bed (I-type).

SOLUTION

• Venn diagram: draw the circle "bed" fully inside the circle "wood". Draw the circle "chair" so that it overlaps (cuts) the circle "bed".

• Conclusion I (Some woods are chair): the part of "chair" that overlaps "bed" also lies inside "wood" (because bed ⊂ wood). So some chair are wood, and by conversion some woods are chair. Follows.

• Conclusion II (Some woods are bed): All bed are wood, and bed exists (it overlaps chair), so at least some wood is bed. Follows (the conversion of an A-type statement gives an I-type statement).

• Both conclusions follow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Syllogism rule: A + I → I (All bed are wood + Some chair are bed → Some chair are wood). An A-type statement always converts to a "Some" statement (All bed are wood → Some wood are bed).

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only conclusion I follows) is wrong because Conclusion II also follows by conversion of "All bed are wood".

• Option 3 (Only conclusion II follows) is wrong because Conclusion I also follows through the common part of bed and chair.

• Option 4 (Either I or II) is wrong because "either-or" applies only when the two conclusions are complementary and neither alone follows. Here both follow definitely.

• Remember: All A are B → Some B are A is a valid conversion for SSC syllogisms.

question: Select the option which is exactly similar to: 788 S. Figueroa St. (Ste. 1900), Los Angeles, CA 90017 — Wed, 12th Aug.
option_1: 788 S. Figueroa St. (Ste. 1900), Los Angeles, CA 90017 — Wed, 12th Aug.
option_2: 788 S. Figueroa St. (Ste 1900), Los Angeles, CA 90017 — Wed, 12th Aug.
option_3: 788 S. Figueroa St. (Ste. 1900), Los Angeles, CA 90017 — Wed, 13th Aug
option_4: 788 S. Figueroa St (Ste. 1900), Los Angeles, CA 90017 — Wed, 12th Aug.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 788 S. Figueroa St. (Ste. 1900), Los Angeles, CA 90017 — Wed, 12th Aug..

GIVEN

• Reference: 788 S. Figueroa St. (Ste. 1900), Los Angeles, CA 90017 — Wed, 12th Aug.

SOLUTION

• Compare the reference with each option, element by element: number, street, suite, city, zip, day-date.

• Option 1: every element and punctuation mark is identical. ✓

• Option 2: "(Ste 1900)" has no full stop after "Ste". ✗

• Option 3: the date is "13th Aug" (not 12th) and the final full stop is missing. ✗

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• In clerical/matching questions, check punctuation marks first (full stops, commas, brackets), then numbers and dates; the first mismatch eliminates an option.

NOTE

• Option 2 differs from the reference: "Ste" instead of "Ste." (missing full stop).

• Option 3 differs: "13th Aug" instead of "12th Aug." (wrong date and missing full stop).

• Option 4 differs: "St" instead of "St." (missing full stop).

• Tip: in "identical / exactly similar" questions, small differences in dots, commas, spellings and digits are the traps.

question:
Identify the identical addresses:

1. Rajiv Kumar Flat-12, Green Valley, Delhi, 110045

2. Rajiv Kumar Flat-12, Green Valley, Delhi, 110045

3. R. Kumar Flat-12, Green Valley, Delhi, 110045

4. Rajiv Kumar Flat-12, Green Valley, New Delhi, 110045
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 1 and 2.

GIVEN

• Four addresses are given; two of them are identical.

SOLUTION

• Address 1: Rajiv Kumar Flat-12, Green Valley, Delhi, 110045

• Address 2: Rajiv Kumar Flat-12, Green Valley, Delhi, 110045 (same as 1 in every word and number)

• Address 3: starts with "R. Kumar" instead of "Rajiv Kumar", so it differs from 1 and 2.

• Address 4: has "New Delhi" instead of "Delhi", so it differs from 1 and 2.

• Hence the identical pair is 1 and 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Compare the name first, then the flat number, locality, city and PIN. Addresses 3 and 4 each break one of these immediately.

NOTE

• Option 2 (2 and 4) is wrong because address 4 has "New Delhi" while address 2 has "Delhi".

• Option 3 (1 and 3) is wrong because address 3 has "R. Kumar" while address 1 has "Rajiv Kumar".

• Option 4 (2 and 3) is wrong for the same reason: "R. Kumar" ≠ "Rajiv Kumar".

• Tip: a single changed word, abbreviation or digit is enough to make two entries non-identical.

question: If 'LOAD' is coded as '3721' and 'DONE' is coded as '1759', how will 'LEND' be coded?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 3951.

GIVEN

• LOAD → 3721 and DONE → 1759. Required: LEND → ?

SOLUTION

• Match the letters of LOAD with the digits of 3721: L = 3, O = 7, A = 2, D = 1.

• Match the letters of DONE with 1759: D = 1 (agrees with the above), O = 7 (agrees), N = 5, E = 9.

• Now code LEND: L = 3, E = 9, N = 5, D = 1 → 3951.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Find the common letters first (D and O appear in both words), fix their digits (D = 1, O = 7), then the remaining letters fall out directly.

NOTE

• Option 2 (4561) uses digits that do not exist in the code table (4, 6 are not assigned to any letter of LOAD or DONE).

• Option 3 (2564) is wrong: 2 is the code for A, which is not in LEND, and 6, 4 are unassigned.

• Option 4 (1987) is wrong: it begins with 1 (= D), but LEND must begin with L = 3.

• Tip: in letter-to-digit coding questions, build a small table of letter = digit and re-use it for the asked word.

question: Complete the series: PMT, OOS, NQR, MSQ, ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. LUP.

GIVEN

• Series: PMT, OOS, NQR, MSQ, ____

SOLUTION

• Take the three letter positions separately.

• First letters: P, O, N, M → each moves 1 step back, so the next is L.

• Second letters: M, O, Q, S → each moves 2 steps forward, so the next is U.

• Third letters: T, S, R, Q → each moves 1 step back, so the next is P.

• The next term is LUP.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Write the position numbers: (16, 13, 20), (15, 15, 19), (14, 17, 18), (13, 19, 17) → changes of −1, +2, −1 in every step, so the next is (12, 21, 16) = L, U, P.

NOTE

• Option 2 (LXP) is wrong: the second letter would be X, a jump of +5 instead of +2.

• Option 3 (LVO) is wrong: the second letter V is a +3 jump and the third letter O is a −2 jump.

• Option 4 (MVP) is wrong: the first letter should fall from M to L, not stay M.

• Tip: for letter series with 3-letter groups, always check each column separately.

question: Complete the series: ACE, GIK, MOQ, ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. SUW.

GIVEN

• Series: ACE, GIK, MOQ, ____

SOLUTION

• Inside each group the letters go up by 2: A, C, E; G, I, K; M, O, Q.

• Between groups the first letter goes up by 6: A → G → M → S.

• So the next group is S, then U (+2), then W (+2) = SUW.

• Position check: ACE = 1, 3, 5; GIK = 7, 9, 11; MOQ = 13, 15, 17; next = 19, 21, 23 = S, U, W.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• The series is just the alphabet taken every second letter (A, C, E, G, I, K, M, O, Q, S, U, W), written three at a time.

NOTE

• Option 2 (TWY): T = 20, W = 23, Y = 25 does not continue the 19, 21, 23 sequence.

• Option 3 (RTS): R = 18, T = 20, S = 19 is not in increasing order at all.

• Option 4 (VXZ): V = 22, X = 24, Z = 26 starts one step too late (22 instead of 19).

• Tip: when the letters in each group form an arithmetic progression, extend the same progression across the whole series.

question:
After interchanging which two numbers (not digits) will the value of the given expression be '81'?

798 + 27 - 719 ÷ 6 x 5
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 798 and 719.

GIVEN

• Expression: 798 + 27 − 719 ÷ 6 × 5. Required value after interchanging two numbers = 81.

SOLUTION

• Interchange 798 and 719: the expression becomes 719 + 27 − 798 ÷ 6 × 5.

• By BODMAS: 798 ÷ 6 = 133, then 133 × 5 = 665.

• Now 719 + 27 − 665 = 746 − 665 = 81 ✓.

• Check the others to be sure: interchanging 5 and 27 gives 798 + 5 − 719 ÷ 6 × 27 ≈ 803 − 3235.5 (negative, not 81); interchanging 5 and 6 gives 798 + 27 − 719 ÷ 5 × 6 = 825 − 862.8 = −37.8; interchanging 27 and 6 gives 798 + 6 − 719 ÷ 27 × 5 ≈ 804 − 133.1 = 670.9.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• The numbers 798 = 6 × 133 and 719 are the only pair that gives whole-number results. Put 719 in front and 798 under the ÷ 6: 746 − 665 = 81.

NOTE

• Option 1 (5 and 27): the value comes out as a large negative decimal, not 81.

• Option 2 (5 and 6): the value is 825 − 862.8 = −37.8, not 81.

• Option 4 (27 and 6): the value is about 670.9, not 81.

• Tip: in "interchange two numbers" questions, look for numbers that divide exactly (here 798 is divisible by 6) to save time.

question: If ÷ denotes addition, × denotes multiplication, + denotes subtraction, and − denotes division, then which of the following equations is correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 15 ÷ 5 × 2 + 6 − 3 = 23.

GIVEN

• ÷ means +, × means ×, + means −, and − means ÷.

SOLUTION

• Replace the symbols in each option with their real meaning and solve by BODMAS.

• Option 2: 15 ÷ 5 × 2 + 6 − 3 → 15 + 5 × 2 − 6 ÷ 3 = 15 + 10 − 2 = 23 ✓ (matches the right side).

• Option 1: 20 × 3 − 5 ÷ 2 + 4 → 20 × 3 ÷ 5 + 2 − 4 = 12 + 2 − 4 = 10 ≠ 34.

• Option 3: 28 + 6 ÷ 2 × 3 − 4 → 28 − 6 + 2 × 3 ÷ 4 = 28 − 6 + 1.5 = 23.5 ≠ 40.

• Option 4: 36 − 12 + 6 ÷ 3 × 2 → 36 ÷ 12 − 6 + 3 × 2 = 3 − 6 + 6 = 3 ≠ 30.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Write a mini conversion table (÷→+, +→−, −→÷, ×→×) and test the option with the neatest numbers first (15, 5, 2, 6, 3 gives clean integers).

NOTE

• Option 1 gives 10, not 34.

• Option 3 gives 23.5, not 40.

• Option 4 gives 3, not 30.

• Remember BODMAS: Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction. Convert the symbols first, then calculate.

question:
Read the four given statements carefully, followed by conclusions I, II, and III. Determine which of the conclusions logically follow from the statements, ignoring any commonly known facts or real-world knowledge.

Statements:

Some cotton clothes are silk clothes.

All silk clothes are woolen clothes.

No woolen cloth is a nylon cloth.

Some nylon clothes are polyester.

Conclusions:

I. Some cotton clothes are nylon clothes

II. No silk cloth is a nylon cloth.

III. Some cotton clothes are woolen clothes.
option_1: Only conclusion I and II follows
option_2: All three conclusion I, II, and III follows
option_3: Only conclusion I and III follows
option_4: Only conclusion II and III follows
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Only conclusion II and III follows.

GIVEN

• S1: Some cotton are silk (I). S2: All silk are woolen (A). S3: No woolen is nylon (E). S4: Some nylon are polyester (I).

SOLUTION

• Venn diagram: draw "silk" fully inside "woolen"; draw "cotton" overlapping "silk"; draw "nylon" completely outside "woolen"; draw "polyester" overlapping "nylon".

• Conclusion I (Some cotton are nylon): nothing connects cotton to nylon. The cotton part we know about lies inside woolen, and nylon is outside woolen. Does not follow.

• Conclusion II (No silk is nylon): silk ⊂ woolen and no woolen is nylon, so A + E → E: No silk is nylon. Follows.

• Conclusion III (Some cotton are woolen): I + A → I: Some cotton are silk, all silk are woolen, so some cotton are woolen. Follows.

• Hence only II and III follow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Use the rules: I + A → I (gives III) and A + E → E (gives II). No rule connects cotton with nylon, so I fails.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only I and II) is wrong because Conclusion I does not follow and Conclusion III does.

• Option 2 (All three) is wrong because Conclusion I does not follow.

• Option 3 (Only I and III) is wrong because Conclusion I does not follow and Conclusion II does.

• Tip: two "Some" statements (cotton–silk and nylon–polyester) never give a conclusion between cotton and nylon.

question: In the following question, a matrix of numbers is given. These numbers follow a certain pattern either row-wise or column-wise. Identify this pattern and choose the missing number accordingly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 10.

GIVEN

• Matrix (rows): (5, 12, ?), (7, 18, 10), (19, 48, 30).

SOLUTION

• Look at the columns. Compute 3 × (first column) − (second column) for the complete rows.

• Row 2: 3 × 7 − 18 = 21 − 18 = 3, and the third column is 10, so 3 = 0.3 × 10.

• Row 3: 3 × 19 − 48 = 57 − 48 = 9, and the third column is 30, so 9 = 0.3 × 30.

• So the rule is: 3 × (first) − (second) = 0.3 × (third), or third = 10 × [3 × first − second] ÷ 3.

• Row 1: 3 × 5 − 12 = 15 − 12 = 3, so 0.3 × ? = 3 → ? = 10.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Test the clean candidate 10 from the options: 3 × 5 − 12 = 3 and 0.3 × 10 = 3, exactly the same as the other two rows (3 and 9 both equal 0.3 × third).

NOTE

• Option 2 (15): 0.3 × 15 = 4.5, but 3 × 5 − 12 = 3. ✗

• Option 3 (18): 0.3 × 18 = 5.4 ≠ 3. ✗

• Option 4 (12): 0.3 × 12 = 3.6 ≠ 3. ✗

• Tip: in matrix questions, try column-wise and row-wise relations such as a × k ± b = c; when one relation fits two complete rows, apply it to the incomplete row.

question: If RAIN is coded as SBLQ, then SNOW is coded as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. TORZ.

GIVEN

• RAIN → SBLQ. Required: SNOW → ?

SOLUTION

• Compare letter by letter: R → S (+1), A → B (+1), I → L (+3), N → Q (+3).

• The shifts are +1, +1, +3, +3.

• Apply to SNOW: S + 1 = T, N + 1 = O, O + 3 = R, W + 3 = Z.

• So SNOW is coded as TORZ.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Write the shifts from the first word (+1, +1, +3, +3) and apply them directly to the new word.

NOTE

• Option 1 (TOSZ): the third letter would be S (O + 4), which breaks the +3 rule.

• Option 2 (TPRZ): the second letter would be P (N + 2), not O (N + 1).

• Option 4 (TNRZ): the second letter would be N (no shift), not O.

• Tip: letter-shift coding usually repeats a short pattern of shifts; find the pattern from the example, then apply it.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term:

GHOST : JCRNW :: FIRED : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. IDUZG.

GIVEN

• GHOST : JCRNW :: FIRED : ?

SOLUTION

• Compare GHOST with JCRNW: G → J (+3), H → C (−5), O → R (+3), S → N (−5), T → W (+3).

• The shifts alternate: +3, −5, +3, −5, +3.

• Apply the same shifts to FIRED: F + 3 = I, I − 5 = D, R + 3 = U, E − 5 = Z (E is 5, minus 5 is 0, so wrap to Z), D + 3 = G.

• The answer is IDUZG.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Only the first two letters are needed to decide: F + 3 = I and I − 5 = D give "ID...", which only Option 3 has.

NOTE

• Option 1 (HCTBG): starts with H (F + 2), which does not match the +3 shift.

• Option 2 (KDGFC): starts with K (F + 5), which does not match the +3 shift.

• Option 4 (IHUDF): the second letter H (I − 1) does not match the −5 shift.

• Tip: when a word is coded with alternating shifts, the shifts can be written as a repeating pair; remember that A − 1 wraps round to Z.

question: If GATE is coded as HaUe, then how is MICE coded?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. NiDe.

GIVEN

• GATE → HaUe. Required: MICE → ?

SOLUTION

• Compare letter by letter: G → H (next letter, capital), A → a (same letter, small), T → U (next letter, capital), E → e (same letter, small).

• Rule: the letters in the 1st and 3rd positions move one step forward and stay capital; the letters in the 2nd and 4th positions stay the same but become small letters.

• Apply to MICE: M → N, I → i, C → D, E → e.

• So MICE is coded as NiDe.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Odd positions: +1 and capital. Even positions: unchanged and small. Only Option 1 follows this (N, i, D, e).

NOTE

• Option 2 (NIdE): the 2nd and 4th letters are written capital and the 3rd is small, the reverse of the code.

• Option 3 (nIdE): even the first letter is small and not shifted, which does not match G → H.

• Option 4 (nidE): the first letter is small and unshifted, and the last is capital, which does not match the code.

• Tip: in case-based codes, record both the letter change and the capital/small change for every position.

question: If A is the son of Q, Q and Y are sisters, Z is the mother of Y, and P is the son of Z, then which of the following statements is correct?
option_2: P is the maternal uncle of A.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. P is the maternal uncle of A..

GIVEN

• A is the son of Q. Q and Y are sisters. Z is the mother of Y. P is the son of Z.

SOLUTION

• Q and Y are sisters and Z is the mother of Y, so Z is also the mother of Q.

• P is the son of Z, so P is the brother of Q and Y.

• A is the son of Q, so P is the brother of A's mother. By definition, a mother's brother is the maternal uncle.

• Therefore P is the maternal uncle of A.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Draw the tree: Z (mother) → children Q, Y, P. Q → child A. A's mother's brother = maternal uncle.

NOTE

• Option 1 (P and A are cousins) is wrong: cousins are children of siblings; P is himself a sibling of A's mother, so he is A's uncle, not cousin.

• Option 3 (Q and P are sisters) is wrong: P is a son, so P and Q are brother and sister.

• Option 4 (A and P are brothers) is wrong: P belongs to the previous generation (A's uncle).

• Tip: mother's brother = maternal uncle; father's brother = paternal uncle.

question:
A delivery executive begins at a central hub and travels 4 km due West. After making a drop-off, he takes a Right turn and drives 9 km North. He then heads East for 12 km to reach a suburban warehouse. His final leg involves a 3 km drive toward the South to reach his destination.

Calculate the straight-line (displacement) distance from the starting hub to his final destination.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 10 km.

GIVEN

• West 4 km → (right turn) North 9 km → East 12 km → South 3 km. Required: straight-line distance from the start.

SOLUTION

• Take the hub as the origin (0, 0). West 4 km → (−4, 0). North 9 km → (−4, 9). East 12 km → (8, 9). South 3 km → (8, 6).

• Net movement: East–West = 8 km towards East (12 − 4); North–South = 6 km towards North (9 − 3).

• Displacement = √(8² + 6²) = √(64 + 36) = √100 = 10 km (a 6-8-10 Pythagorean triplet).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Add up the opposite directions: East 12 − West 4 = 8; North 9 − South 3 = 6; recognise the triplet (6, 8, 10).

NOTE

• Option 1 (15 km) is wrong: it is not a possible resultant of 8 km and 6 km (it would need a perpendicular pair like 9 and 12).

• Option 2 (13 km) is wrong: it comes from a 5-12-13 triplet, which does not apply here.

• Option 4 (8 km) is wrong: it is only the East component and ignores the 6 km northward shift.

• Tip: direction questions always reduce to net East–West and net North–South distances, then use Pythagoras.

question:
Instruction: The question given below is followed by two statements I and II. Determine which statement(s) is/are sufficient to answer the question.

Question: Who is the tallest among H, M, and K?

Statements:

I. H is taller than M but shorter than K.

II. M is not taller than K.
option_3: Both I and II together are sufficient
option_4: Either I or II is sufficient
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only I is sufficient.

GIVEN

• Question: Who is the tallest among H, M and K?

SOLUTION

• Statement I: H > M and H < K, so K > H > M. K is clearly the tallest. Sufficient.

• Statement II: M is not taller than K (M ≤ K). This says nothing about H, so H could be taller than K or shorter. Not sufficient.

• Therefore only Statement I is sufficient.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Arrange the order of heights from each statement separately. If the whole order (or at least the top person) is fixed, it is sufficient.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Only II) is wrong: II compares only M and K, so H's height is unknown.

• Option 3 (Both together) is wrong: Statement I alone already answers the question, so both are not needed.

• Option 4 (Either I or II) is wrong: II alone does not answer the question.

• Tip: "not taller" means shorter or equal; this can leave the tallest person undecided.

question: In the following question, a matrix is given. A relationship exists among the elements in each row/column. Study the pattern and choose the alternative that will replace the "?".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• Matrix rows: (3, 6, 2), (4, 20, 5), (6, 18, ?).

SOLUTION

• Row 1: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 (second ÷ first = third).

• Row 2: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 (second ÷ first = third).

• Row 3: 18 ÷ 6 = 3, so the missing number is 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• In each row, third number = second ÷ first, or equivalently first × third = second (3 × 2 = 6, 4 × 5 = 20, 6 × 3 = 18).

NOTE

• Option 2 (6): 6 × 6 = 36, not 18. ✗

• Option 3 (48): 6 × 48 = 288, not 18. ✗

• Option 4 (24): 6 × 24 = 144, not 18. ✗

• Tip: in row-wise matrices, test the simple operations first: a + b = c, a × b = c, b ÷ a = c, a × c = b.

question:
In the following question, evaluate the statement and select the valid conclusion.

Statements:

I. Excessive consumption of sugar can lead to diabetes.

II. Diabetes affects the normal functioning of the human body.

Conclusions:

I. Sugar intake should be limited.

II. All people who eat sugar will get diabetes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only conclusion I follows..

GIVEN

• Statement I: Excessive sugar consumption can lead to diabetes. Statement II: Diabetes affects the normal functioning of the body.

SOLUTION

• Conclusion I (Sugar intake should be limited): since too much sugar can lead to diabetes, and diabetes harms the body, limiting sugar intake is a reasonable course of action that follows from the statements. Follows.

• Conclusion II (All people who eat sugar will get diabetes): the statement says only that excessive consumption can lead to diabetes. "All" and "will" are too strong. Does not follow.

• Therefore only Conclusion I follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Be wary of absolute words such as "all", "will", "only", "never" in a conclusion when the statement uses softer words such as "can", "may", "some".

NOTE

• Option 2 (Only II) is wrong: the statement does not say that all sugar eaters get diabetes.

• Option 3 (Both) is wrong because Conclusion II does not follow.

• Option 4 (Neither) is wrong because Conclusion I (limit sugar) is supported by the statements.

• Tip: in "course of action" type conclusions, "should" conclusions are accepted only when the statements give a clear harm or benefit to act upon.

question:
In the following question, evaluate the statement and select the valid conclusion.

Statements:

I. Vaccination helps the body develop immunity against diseases.

II. Many deadly diseases can be prevented by vaccination.

Conclusions:

I. Vaccination is important for public health.

II. Vaccinated people never fall ill.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only conclusion I follows..

GIVEN

• Statements: vaccination builds immunity; many deadly diseases can be prevented by vaccination.

SOLUTION

• Conclusion I (Vaccination is important for public health): if vaccination develops immunity and prevents many deadly diseases, it clearly protects the health of the public. Follows.

• Conclusion II (Vaccinated people never fall ill): the statements say diseases "can be prevented" and immunity is "helped". They do not claim 100% protection, and "never" is an absolute word. Does not follow.

• So only Conclusion I follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Absolute words ("never", "always", "all", "only") in a conclusion are the usual trap; the statements use only soft words ("helps", "many", "can").

NOTE

• Option 2 (Only II) is wrong: "never fall ill" is too strong and unsupported.

• Option 3 (Both) is wrong because Conclusion II does not follow.

• Option 4 (Neither) is wrong because Conclusion I follows directly from the benefits mentioned.

• Tip: prefer moderate conclusions that restate the benefit or harm mentioned in the statements.

question:
In the following question, evaluate the statement and select the valid conclusion.

Statements:

I. Antibiotics are effective only against bacterial infections and not viral infections.

II. Many people take antibiotics even during common viral illnesses like cold and flu.

Conclusions:

I. Misuse of antibiotics can lead to antibiotic resistance.

II. Antibiotics should be used for all types of infections to recover faster.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Neither I nor II follows..

GIVEN

• Statement I: Antibiotics work only against bacterial infections, not viral ones. Statement II: Many people take antibiotics even for cold and flu (viral illnesses).

SOLUTION

• Conclusion I (Misuse of antibiotics can lead to antibiotic resistance): the statements talk about the ineffectiveness of antibiotics against viruses and about people taking them wrongly, but they say nothing about "resistance". Antibiotic resistance is outside information, and the instructions say to judge only from the statements. Does not follow (as per the key).

• Conclusion II (Antibiotics should be used for all types of infections): this directly contradicts Statement I, which says antibiotics are not effective against viral infections. Does not follow.

• So neither conclusion follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Check each conclusion against the statements only. If the key word of a conclusion (here "resistance") is never mentioned in the statements, it does not follow; if it contradicts a statement, it never follows.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only I) is wrong in this paper's key because "antibiotic resistance" is not stated or logically implied by the two statements. (In real life resistance is a known risk, which is why this item is often debated.)

• Option 2 (Only II) is wrong because it contradicts Statement I.

• Option 3 (Both) is wrong because Conclusion II contradicts Statement I.

• The answer follows the key given in the PDF (Option 4). Flagged for the reader: Conclusion I is a true real-world fact, so some aspirants may argue for Option 1.

question:
In the following question, read the statement and select the valid  assumptions

Statement:

The company has increased salaries to retain skilled employees.

Assumptions:

I. Skilled employees were leaving the company earlier.

II. Salary increase is the only way to retain employees.
option_3: Both I and II are implicit
option_4: Neither I nor II is implicit
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only assumption I is implicit..

GIVEN

• Statement: The company has increased salaries to retain skilled employees.

SOLUTION

• An assumption is an unstated belief that must be true for the statement to make sense.

• Assumption I (Skilled employees were leaving earlier): a company tries to "retain" employees when it fears or faces their departure. So this is implicit.

• Assumption II (Salary increase is the only way): the company chose one way; this does not mean it believes there is no other way (training, promotions, benefits could also work). Not implicit.

• Hence only Assumption I is implicit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Words like "only", "all" and "never" in an assumption usually make it invalid, while an assumption that explains the reason for the action in the statement is usually valid.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Only II) is wrong: the statement does not say that salary is the sole way.

• Option 3 (Both) is wrong because II is not implicit.

• Option 4 (Neither) is wrong because I is implicit: retention implies a risk of leaving.

• Tip: assumption = "taken for granted"; inference = "drawn from"; do not confuse them.

question:
In the following question, one statement is given, followed by certain inferences. Consider the statement to be true even if it seems to contradict commonly known facts. Read the inferences carefully and decide which of them logically follow(s) from the given statement.

Statement:

Providing regular training to employees increases organizational productivity.

Inferences:

I. Trained employees are likely to perform better at work.

II. Productivity cannot increase without regular employee training.
option_3: Both inference I and inference II follow
option_4: Neither inference I nor inference II follow
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only inference I follows.

GIVEN

• Statement: Providing regular training to employees increases organizational productivity.

SOLUTION

• Inference I (Trained employees are likely to perform better): training raises productivity, which comes from better employee performance. This is a reasonable, probable inference. Follows.

• Inference II (Productivity cannot increase without regular training): the statement says training is one way to increase productivity; it does not say it is the only way. Does not follow.

• Therefore only Inference I follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• "X increases Y" does not mean "Y cannot increase without X". Reversing a cause into a necessary condition is a classic trap.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Only II) is wrong: II treats training as the only cause, which is not stated.

• Option 3 (Both) is wrong because II does not follow.

• Option 4 (Neither) is wrong because I follows from the link between training and productivity.

• Tip: inferences with phrases like "likely", "probably" are safer than those with "cannot", "only", "always".

question:
X is the son of Y. R is the father of Q and A. A is the daughter of Y.

How is A related to X?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Sister.

GIVEN

• X is the son of Y. R is the father of Q and A. A is the daughter of Y.

SOLUTION

• X is the son of Y, and A is the daughter of the same Y, so X and A are children of the same parent.

• A is female (daughter), X is male (son). Hence A is the sister of X.

• (R is the father of A, so R is the father of both A and her sibling X's parent Y's partner; the information about Q and R is extra.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Same parent + female child = sister; same parent + male child = brother.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Mother) is wrong: A is a daughter of Y, so she is on the same generation as X, not above.

• Option 2 (Aunt) is wrong: an aunt would be a sister of X's parent, not the daughter of Y.

• Option 3 (Daughter) is wrong: X and A are both children of Y; A is not X's child.

• Tip: ignore extra, irrelevant statements (about R and Q here); they are given to distract.

question: BIMSTEC mainly promotes cooperation among countries surrounding which body of water?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bay of Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• BIMSTEC stands for the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation. It links the countries lying on or near the Bay of Bengal (बंगाल की खाड़ी).

 

• It was founded on 6 June 1997 through the Bangkok Declaration (originally BIST-EC with Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand). Myanmar joined in December 1997, and Nepal and Bhutan joined in 2004.

 

• It has seven members: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. Its Secretariat is in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

 

• It bridges South Asia and South-East Asia and is seen as an alternative to SAARC for regional cooperation, especially after India's "Neighbourhood First" and "Act East" policies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The BIMSTEC Charter was adopted at the 5th Summit (Colombo, 2022); the 6th Summit was held in Bangkok in April 2025, where the chair passed to Bangladesh.

 

• Sectoral cooperation is shared among member states (for example, India leads areas such as security and counter-terrorism). The BIMSTEC Day is celebrated on 6 June.

 

• SAARC (1985) has eight members and its Secretariat is in Kathmandu; ASEAN (1967) has its Secretariat in Jakarta.

 

NOTE

 

• Arabian Sea (Option 1) is wrong: it lies on India's west coast and is not the focus of BIMSTEC; the countries around it are linked more with the Indian Ocean Rim groupings.

 

• South China Sea (Option 3) is wrong: it is a disputed sea in East/South-East Asia and has no link with BIMSTEC's name or membership.

 

• Indian Ocean (Option 4) is wrong: it is far larger and the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) is the grouping named after it. BIMSTEC is specifically about the Bay of Bengal region.

question: The Global Innovation Index (GII) 2025 is released by which organization?
solution_text:
The correct answer is World Intellectual Property Organization.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Global Innovation Index (GII) is published every year by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) (विश्व बौद्धिक संपदा संगठन), a specialised agency of the United Nations headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

 

• The index ranks the innovation performance of about 130 economies using indicators on institutions, human capital and research, infrastructure, market and business sophistication, and knowledge and creative outputs.

 

• Switzerland has been at the top of the GII for many years; India has been moving up the ranking (39th in 2024 and 38th in 2025).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• WIPO was established in 1967 (the convention came into force in 1970) and became a UN specialised agency in 1974. Its head is called the Director General.

 

• Other well-known indices and who publishes them: Human Development Index (UNDP), Global Gender Gap Report (WEF), World Economic Outlook (IMF), World Happiness Report (UN SDSN), Global Hunger Index (Welthungerhilfe and Concern Worldwide).

 

NOTE

 

• World Economic Forum (Option 1) is wrong: WEF publishes the Global Gender Gap Report, Global Risks Report and Travel & Tourism Development Index, not the GII.

 

• United Nations Development Programme (Option 3) is wrong: UNDP publishes the Human Development Report and Human Development Index.

 

• International Monetary Fund (Option 4) is wrong: the IMF publishes the World Economic Outlook and other financial reports.

question: Which country ranked as the happiest in the world for the ninth consecutive year in the World Happiness Report 2026?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Finland.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Finland (फिनलैंड) was ranked the happiest country in the world for the ninth consecutive year in the World Happiness Report 2026. It has topped the report every year since 2018.

 

• The World Happiness Report is published by the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN), together with partners such as the Gallup World Poll, and is released around 20 March each year on the International Day of Happiness.

 

• Rankings are based on a three-year average of life evaluations by citizens (the Cantril ladder) and are explained with six factors: GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity and perceptions of corruption.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nordic countries (Finland, Denmark, Iceland, Sweden, Norway) regularly appear in the top ten. In the 2025 report the top order was Finland, Denmark, Iceland and Sweden.

 

• The International Day of Happiness is observed on 20 March (declared by the UN General Assembly in 2012). Bhutan's "Gross National Happiness" idea inspired this movement.

 

NOTE

 

• Iceland (Option 2) is wrong: Iceland is a regular top-five country but has not held the top rank.

 

• Denmark (Option 3) is wrong: Denmark was second in the 2025 report and has held the top spot only in earlier years (before 2018).

 

• Sweden (Option 4) is wrong: Sweden is usually in the top ten but not first.

question: PSLV-C62 was launched from which location?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sriharikota.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The PSLV-C62 mission carrying the earth observation satellite EOS-N1 (with several co-passenger payloads) was launched in January 2026 from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), Sriharikota (श्रीहरिकोटा), Andhra Pradesh. It was ISRO's first launch of 2026.

 

• Sriharikota is a barrier island on the east coast of India, about 80 km north of Chennai, and is India's main orbital launch port (SHAR). It is named after Satish Dhawan, a former ISRO chairman.

 

• PSLV stands for Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle; it is a four-stage vehicle (alternating solid and liquid stages) and is ISRO's reliable workhorse.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala) launched India's first sounding rocket in 1963; the Kulasekarapattinam spaceport in Tamil Nadu is being developed for small satellite launches.

 

• ISRO was formed in 1969 and has its headquarters in Bengaluru; its chairman is also Secretary, Department of Space.

 

NOTE

 

• Thumba (Option 1) is wrong: it is a sounding-rocket launch station, not the site of orbital launches.

 

• Mahendragiri (Option 3) is wrong: it is the ISRO Propulsion Complex in Tamil Nadu used for testing liquid and cryogenic engines, not for launching.

 

• Balasore (Option 4) is wrong: it is in Odisha and hosts the DRDO missile test range (Chandipur / Abdul Kalam Island), not an ISRO orbital launch pad.

question:
Fill in the blank:

According to the 2011 Census, India's total population is___ million.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1,210 million.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the 2011 Census, India's total population was 1,210,854,977, i.e. about 1,210 million (1.21 billion) (भारत की जनगणना 2011).

 

• Males numbered about 623.7 million and females about 586.5 million, giving a sex ratio of 943 females per 1000 males. The decadal growth rate (2001–2011) was 17.64% and the population density was 382 persons per sq km.

 

• India's literacy rate in 2011 was 74.04%. Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state and Sikkim the least populous.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala has the highest sex ratio (1084) and Haryana the lowest among major states (879). Bihar has the highest density among states (1106 per sq km).

 

• The Census is conducted every ten years under the Census Act, 1948 (the first Census was in 1872 and the first complete Census in 1881). The Census of India is under the Ministry of Home Affairs (Registrar General and Census Commissioner).

 

NOTE

 

• 1,028 million (Option 1) is wrong: this is the population of the 2001 Census (about 1,028.7 million).

 

• 3,287 million (Option 3) is wrong: 3,287,263 sq km is the area of India (not the population).

 

• 1,350 million (Option 4) is wrong: it is a later estimate of population, not the 2011 Census figure.

question:
Fill in the blank:

The budget document showing only current receipts and current expenditure is called the _ budget.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Revenue budget.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Revenue Budget (राजस्व बजट) shows the revenue receipts of the government (tax revenue and non-tax revenue) and the revenue expenditure (day-to-day running costs such as salaries, interest, subsidies and pensions).

 

• Revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce an asset of the government. Revenue expenditure does not create any asset for the government.

 

• Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure − Revenue receipts. A revenue deficit means the government is spending more than it earns on current account.

 

• Under Article 112 of the Constitution the President lays before Parliament the Annual Financial Statement (the Budget) each year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Budget has two parts: the Revenue Budget and the Capital Budget. The Capital Budget deals with capital receipts (borrowings, recovery of loans, disinvestment) and capital expenditure (building roads, dams, purchase of assets).

 

• Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts). Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit − Interest payments.

 

• The Union Budget is presented on 1 February (since 2017, the Railway Budget was merged with the General Budget).

 

NOTE

 

• Capital budget (Option 1) is wrong: it covers capital receipts and capital expenditure, not current receipts and current expenditure.

 

• Balanced budget (Option 3) is wrong: it means estimated receipts equal estimated expenditure; it is not defined by "current" items.

 

• Performance budget (Option 4) is wrong: it links the money spent on a programme with the results or performance expected (introduced in India in 1968-69).

question: Which indicator measures the total value of final goods and services produced within a country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gross Domestic Product.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gross Domestic Product (GDP) (सकल घरेलू उत्पाद) is the total market value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country in a given period (usually one year), whether by nationals or foreigners.

 

• Only final goods are counted to avoid double counting of intermediate goods.

 

• GDP at market price = GDP at factor cost + indirect taxes − subsidies.

 

• GDP can be measured by three methods: the production (value added) method, the income method and the expenditure method.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA). GNP therefore counts what the residents of a country produce, wherever they are.

 

• NNP = GNP − Depreciation (capital consumption allowance). National Income = NNP at factor cost.

 

• In India, GDP data is released by the National Statistics Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

 

NOTE

 

• Gross National Product (Option 1) is wrong: it includes income earned by residents from abroad and excludes foreigners' income earned within the country (that is, GDP plus net factor income from abroad).

 

• Net National Product (Option 2) is wrong: it is GNP minus depreciation, not a measure of production within the country.

 

• Personal Income (Option 4) is wrong: it is the income actually received by individuals (including transfer payments) before income tax.

question: Which committee was set up in 1955 to highlight and promote the role of small-scale industries for rural development?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karve Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Karve Committee (कर्वे समिति) was set up in 1955 (formally the Village and Small-Scale Industries Committee, headed by D. G. Karve) to suggest how village and small-scale industries could be developed to create rural employment.

 

• It stressed decentralised production, labour-intensive industries in rural areas and the use of cottage and village industries for balanced regional development.

 

• Its thinking shaped the industrial policy of the Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61) and the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), which was set up in 1957 under the KVIC Act, 1956.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Small-scale industries received support in the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 (the "economic constitution of India"), and the Small Industries Development Organisation (SIDO) and National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC) were set up to support them.

 

• Today MSMEs are governed by the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006, and classified on the basis of investment and turnover.

 

NOTE

 

• Narasimham Committee (Option 1) is wrong: it is associated with banking and financial sector reforms (1991 and 1998).

 

• Tendulkar Committee (Option 3) is wrong: it is associated with the estimation of poverty (2009).

 

• Kelkar Committee (Option 4) is wrong: it is associated with tax reforms and fiscal consolidation.

question: Which category of evidence is required to be 'direct' under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Spoken Oral evidence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 (भारतीय साक्ष्य अधिनियम), oral evidence must in all cases be direct (Section 55, which corresponds to Section 60 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872).

 

• "Direct" means: if the fact refers to something that could be seen, it must be the evidence of the witness who says he saw it; if it could be heard, of the witness who heard it; if it could be perceived by any other sense, of the witness who perceived it by that sense; and if it is an opinion, the person who holds that opinion.

 

• So hearsay (what someone was told by another person) is, as a general rule, not accepted as oral evidence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The BSA, 2023 replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 and came into force on 1 July 2024, together with the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (replacing the IPC) and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (replacing the CrPC).

 

• It recognises electronic and digital records as documents, and electronic records are admissible as primary evidence in the manner prescribed (with a certificate under Section 63, which corresponds to Section 65B of the Evidence Act).

 

NOTE

 

• Documentary evidence (Option 1) is wrong: documents are proved by primary or secondary evidence; the rule of "direct" evidence applies to oral evidence.

 

• Electronic evidence (Option 3) is wrong: electronic records are treated as documents and are proved by the rules on documents and the certificate.

 

• Secondary evidence (Option 4) is wrong: secondary evidence (copies, oral accounts of a document's contents) is allowed only in the cases listed in the Act when primary evidence is not available.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the applicability of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023:

1. It is applicable to all judicial proceedings in or before any Court, including Courts-martial.

2. It is strictly applicable to affidavits presented to any Court or officer.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 applies to all judicial proceedings in or before any Court, including Courts-martial (न्यायालयों और कोर्ट-मार्शल में सभी न्यायिक कार्यवाहियाँ).

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect: the Act specifically does not apply to affidavits presented to any Court or officer, nor to proceedings before an arbitrator. So the word "strictly applicable" is wrong.

 

• The Act is divided into 12 chapters and has 170 sections (the Evidence Act, 1872 had 167).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rules on the relevancy of facts, the proof of facts, the production of witnesses and the burden of proof are contained in the Act. Section 1 deals with the short title and the application.

 

• The Bill was passed by Parliament in December 2023, received the President's assent on 25 December 2023 and came into force on 1 July 2024.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (2 only) is wrong: Statement 2 is incorrect because affidavits are excluded.

 

• Option 3 (Both 1 and 2) is wrong: only Statement 1 is correct.

 

• Option 4 (Neither) is wrong: Statement 1 is correct.

question: Which of the following groups correctly represents any three of the six Vedangas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Siksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The six Vedangas (वेदांग — "limbs of the Veda") are auxiliary disciplines needed to read, recite and understand the Vedas correctly: Shiksha (phonetics), Kalpa (ritual), Vyakarana (grammar), Nirukta (etymology), Chhanda (metre) and Jyotisha (astronomy/astrology).

 

• Option 1 (Siksha, Kalpa, Vyakarana) contains three genuine Vedangas, so it is correct.

 

• Panini's Ashtadhyayi is the best-known work on Vyakarana, Yaska's Nirukta explains Vedic words, and Pingala's Chhandahsutra deals with metre.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vedic literature has four Samhitas (Rig, Sama, Yajur, Atharva), followed by the Brahmanas, Aranyakas and Upanishads. The Vedangas are not part of the Vedas themselves but aids to them.

 

• The Upavedas are Ayurveda, Dhanurveda, Gandharvaveda and Arthashastra/Shilpaveda.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (Nirukta, Arthashastra, Smriti) is wrong: Arthashastra and Smriti are not Vedangas (Kautilya's Arthashastra is a treatise on statecraft).

 

• Option 3 (Chhanda, Purana, Upanishad) is wrong: Purana and Upanishad are not Vedangas.

 

• Option 4 (Jyotisha, Brahmana, Aranyaka) is wrong: Brahmana and Aranyaka are parts of the Vedic literature itself, not Vedangas.

question: Which of the following sets consists only of non-metallic minerals commonly used within local markets in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Limestone, dolomite, phosphate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Minerals are classified into metallic (ferrous and non-ferrous), non-metallic and energy (fuel) minerals.

 

• Limestone, dolomite and phosphate (चूना पत्थर, डोलोमाइट, फॉस्फेट) are all non-metallic minerals and are widely used in cement, steel flux, fertilisers and construction. So Option 1 consists only of non-metallic minerals.

 

• Other non-metallic minerals of India: mica (Jharkhand, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan), gypsum (Rajasthan), salt, asbestos, kyanite and sillimanite.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh are leading producers of limestone, and Rajasthan dominates in gypsum. India is a leading producer of mica.

 

• Mining and mineral development is governed by the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 (MMDR Act); the Ministry of Mines is the nodal ministry.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (Coal, petroleum, natural gas) is wrong: these are energy (fossil fuel) minerals, usually classified separately from metallic and non-metallic minerals. (They are non-metallic in the chemical sense, but the standard classification used in exams keeps them as a separate fuel category; the key of the paper is Option 1.)

 

• Option 3 (Copper, aluminium, iron) is wrong: all three are metals (metallic minerals or their ores).

 

• Option 4 (Uranium, thorium, copper) is wrong: uranium and thorium are atomic/energy minerals and copper is a metal.

question: In the Hershey-Chase experiment, why were some bacteria found to be radioactive only when infected with viruses grown on a medium containing Radioactive Phosphorus (³⁵P)?
option_1: Phosphorus is found in the protein coat of the virus.
option_2: Phosphorus is a constituent of DNA but not of proteins.
option_3: Sulfur is a constituent of DNA but phosphorus is not.
option_4: The virus injected its protein coat into the bacterial cell.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Phosphorus is a constituent of DNA but not of proteins..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Hershey-Chase experiment (1952), Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase used bacteriophage T2 (a virus that infects bacteria) to show that DNA is the genetic material.

 

• DNA contains phosphorus (in its sugar-phosphate backbone) but no sulfur. Proteins contain sulfur (in amino acids such as cysteine and methionine) but almost no phosphorus.

 

• Viruses grown with radioactive phosphorus labelled their DNA, and the infected bacteria became radioactive because the viral DNA entered the bacterial cell. Viruses grown with radioactive sulfur (³⁵S) labelled the protein coat, which stayed outside, so the bacteria were not radioactive.

 

• Hence the reason is that phosphorus is a constituent of DNA but not of proteins.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Note: in the actual experiment the isotope used for DNA was ³²P and for the protein coat ³⁵S; the question as printed writes ³⁵P, which is a misprint (flagged in the verification report). The answer is not affected.

 

• Earlier experiments: Griffith's transformation experiment (1928) and Avery, MacLeod and McCarty (1944) also pointed to DNA. Watson and Crick proposed the double helix model in 1953.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is wrong: the protein coat of a virus contains sulfur, not phosphorus.

 

• Option 3 is wrong: sulfur is a constituent of proteins, not of DNA, and phosphorus is a key part of DNA.

 

• Option 4 is wrong: the virus injected its DNA, not its protein coat; the empty protein coats (ghosts) remained outside the bacterium.

question: The term "nife" used for the earth's core refers to the dominance of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nickel and iron.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nife (निफे) is the name given to the earth's core (barysphere). It is made up mainly of nickel (Ni) and iron (Fe) — "Ni" + "Fe".

 

• The core begins at a depth of about 2,900 km and extends to the centre at about 6,371 km. The outer core is liquid and the inner core is solid; the core's density is about 13 g/cm³ and its temperature is very high (around 5,000 °C or more).

 

• The movement of the liquid outer core is responsible for the earth's magnetic field.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sial (silica + alumina) forms the continental crust; Sima (silica + magnesium) forms the oceanic crust and lies below the sial. The mantle is also called the "mesosphere" and consists of silicate rocks rich in iron and magnesium.

 

• The Mohorovicic discontinuity (Moho) separates the crust from the mantle, and the Gutenberg discontinuity separates the mantle from the core.

 

NOTE

 

• Nickel and feldspar (Option 1) is wrong: feldspar is a rock-forming silicate mineral of the crust.

 

• Nitrogen and iron (Option 2) is wrong: nitrogen is not a constituent of the core; the symbol "Ni" stands for nickel.

 

• Sodium and iron (Option 4) is wrong: sodium is a light element found in the crust, not in the core.

question: The term "Jujutsu" is the foundational martial art for which Olympic sport?

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

question: Which of the following terms is used in Athletics specifically for the exchange of a baton between two runners?

question: Which Indian scientist is known as the 'Father of Fiber Optics' for his pioneering work in the transmission of light through glass fibers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narinder Singh Kapany.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Narinder Singh Kapany (नरिंदर सिंह कपानी) (1926–2020), an Indian-born American physicist born in Moga, Punjab, is called the "Father of Fiber Optics". He demonstrated the transmission of light through bent glass fibres in the 1950s and coined the term "fiber optics" in a 1960 article in Scientific American.

 

• Fibre optics works on the principle of total internal reflection of light inside a thin glass or plastic fibre. It is used in telecommunications, internet cables and medical endoscopy.

 

• Fortune magazine named him one of the seven "unsung heroes" of the 20th century (1999), and he was awarded the Padma Bhushan (2021, posthumous) and earlier the Padma Vibhushan (2021).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

• Charles Kao (Nobel Prize in Physics, 2009) is called the "Father of Fibre-Optic Communications" for his work on low-loss fibres.

question: Which eminent Indian scientist founded the 'Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science' (IACS) in Kolkata?

question:

question: Which medieval Indian ruler is often called the 'Precursor of Akbar' for his administrative and land revenue reforms?
solution_text:

• He introduced a systematic land survey and measurement, fixed the land revenue at about one-third of the produce, gave farmers patta (title deed) and took qabuliyat (agreement). Todar Mal worked under him and later served Akbar.

 

• He built the Grand Trunk Road (Sonargaon to Peshawar), rest houses (sarais), and issued the silver rupaya and copper dam; he introduced a cash-based system.

 

• He defeated Humayun at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj/Bilgram (1540). His tomb is at Sasaram, Bihar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

question: According to the Food and Agriculture Organisation-Global Forest Resources Assessment report 2025, what is India's global rank in terms of total forest area?

question: Which of the following is one of the stated objectives of the Green Credit Programme?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Restore degraded lands.

• Its activities include tree plantation and restoration of degraded land, water conservation and harvesting, sustainable agriculture, waste management and sustainable building practices. A green credit is issued for each such activity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

question: If x = 531, y = -295 and z = -231, find the value of [(x-y)² + (y - z)² + (z - x)²] / (x³ + y³ + z³ - 3xyz).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 0.4.

GIVEN

• x = 531, y = −295, z = −231. Expression = [(x − y)² + (y − z)² + (z − x)²] ÷ (x³ + y³ + z³ − 3xyz).

SOLUTION

• Identity 1: (x − y)² + (y − z)² + (z − x)² = 2(x² + y² + z² − xy − yz − zx).

• Identity 2: x³ + y³ + z³ − 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x² + y² + z² − xy − yz − zx).

• Dividing, the common factor cancels: expression = 2(x² + y² + z² − xy − yz − zx) ÷ [(x + y + z)(x² + y² + z² − xy − yz − zx)] = 2 ÷ (x + y + z).

• x + y + z = 531 − 295 − 231 = 5.

• So the value = 2 ÷ 5 = 0.4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Whenever you see this fraction, the answer is simply 2 ÷ (x + y + z); only the sum of the three numbers is needed.

NOTE

• Option 1 (0.6) would need x + y + z = 3.33, which does not match the sum 5.

• Option 3 (0.5) would need the sum to be 4. ✗

• Option 4 (0.3) would need the sum to be 6.67. ✗

• Remember: if x + y + z = 0, then x³ + y³ + z³ = 3xyz (the denominator becomes 0 and the fraction is undefined).

question: Ravi started a business with an investment of Rs. 90,000 and after 4 months Krishna joined him investing Rs. 1,50,000. If the profit at the end of the year is Rs. 66,500, then find Krishna's profit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Rs. 35,000.

GIVEN

• Ravi: Rs. 90,000 for 12 months. Krishna: Rs. 1,50,000 for 12 − 4 = 8 months. Total profit = Rs. 66,500.

SOLUTION

• Profit is shared in the ratio of (investment × time).

• Ravi : Krishna = (90,000 × 12) : (1,50,000 × 8) = 10,80,000 : 12,00,000 = 9 : 10.

• Total parts = 9 + 10 = 19.

• Krishna's share = (10 ÷ 19) × 66,500 = 10 × 3,500 = Rs. 35,000.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Cancel common factors early: (9 × 12) : (15 × 8) = 108 : 120 = 9 : 10. Since 66,500 ÷ 19 = 3,500, Krishna gets 10 × 3,500 = 35,000.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Rs. 31,500) is Ravi's share (9 × 3,500), not Krishna's.

• Option 3 (Rs. 27,500) and Option 4 (Rs. 21,500) do not correspond to any whole-number parts of the 9 : 10 ratio.

• Formula: Profit ratio = (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂).

question: At what rate per annum will Rs. 54,000 yield a compound interest of Rs. 39,312 in 9 months compounded quarterly?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 80%.

GIVEN

• Principal P = Rs. 54,000; compound interest = Rs. 39,312; time = 9 months = 3 quarters; compounded quarterly.

SOLUTION

• Amount A = P + CI = 54,000 + 39,312 = Rs. 93,312.

• A ÷ P = 93,312 ÷ 54,000 = 1.728 = (1.2)³.

• For quarterly compounding, A = P(1 + r/4 ÷ 100)³, so 1 + (quarterly rate)/100 = 1.2, which means the quarterly rate = 20%.

• Annual rate = 20 × 4 = 80% per annum.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Recognise 1.728 as 1.2³ (memorise cubes: 1.1³ = 1.331, 1.2³ = 1.728, 1.3³ = 2.197). The quarterly rate is 20%, so the yearly rate is 20 × 4 = 80%.

NOTE

• Option 1 (45%): quarterly 11.25%, A = 54,000 × 1.1125³ ≈ 74,350, not 93,312.

• Option 2 (54%): quarterly 13.5%, A = 54,000 × 1.135³ ≈ 78,960, not 93,312.

• Option 3 (72%): quarterly 18%, A = 54,000 × 1.18³ ≈ 88,720, not 93,312.

• Formula for compounding in parts of a year: A = P[1 + (R/n)/100]^(nT), where n is the number of times interest is compounded in a year.

question: Raj purchases an item whose marked price is partly paid in cash and the balance through a credit card. On the cash-paid 30% portion, he receives a 35% discount, while the credit-card-paid 70% portion incurs a 3% surcharge. If the total amount he finally pays is ₹9,160. Find the marked price of the item?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ₹10,000.

GIVEN

• Cash part = 30% of marked price (MP) with 35% discount. Credit-card part = 70% of MP with 3% surcharge. Final payment = ₹9,160.

SOLUTION

• Let the marked price be MP.

• Cash portion pays: 0.30 × MP × (1 − 0.35) = 0.30 × 0.65 × MP = 0.195 MP.

• Credit-card portion pays: 0.70 × MP × (1 + 0.03) = 0.70 × 1.03 × MP = 0.721 MP.

• Total = 0.195 MP + 0.721 MP = 0.916 MP = 9,160.

• MP = 9,160 ÷ 0.916 = ₹10,000.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Take MP = 100: pays 30 × 0.65 + 70 × 1.03 = 19.5 + 72.1 = 91.6. So the final payment is 91.6% of MP; MP = 9,160 ÷ 0.916 = 10,000.

NOTE

• Option 1 (₹7,500) would give a final payment of 0.916 × 7,500 = ₹6,870. ✗

• Option 2 (₹8,500) would give 0.916 × 8,500 = ₹7,786. ✗

• Option 3 (₹9,000) would give 0.916 × 9,000 = ₹8,244. ✗

• Tip: convert every discount/surcharge to a multiplier (0.65 and 1.03) and add the weighted parts.

question: A bottle contains 80 lit of a honey-water mixture and 25% of the mixture is pure honey. Some additional pure honey is added to the bottle so that the final mixture contains 60% honey. What amount of pure honey must be added to achieve this new concentration?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 70 lit.

GIVEN

• Mixture = 80 litres with 25% honey, so honey = 20 litres and water = 60 litres. Final concentration = 60% honey.

SOLUTION

• Water stays the same (60 litres) and in the final mixture water is 100% − 60% = 40%.

• Final mixture = 60 ÷ 0.40 = 150 litres.

• Honey added = 150 − 80 = 70 litres.

• Check by equation: (20 + x) ÷ (80 + x) = 0.6, so 20 + x = 48 + 0.6x, which gives 0.4x = 28 and x = 70. ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• When only one component is added, the other component is constant: water 60 L = 40% of the new total, so the new total = 150 L and the honey added = 150 − 80 = 70 L.

NOTE

• Option 1 (50 lit): honey = 70 L in 130 L = 53.8%, not 60%.

• Option 2 (90 lit): honey = 110 L in 170 L = 64.7%, not 60%.

• Option 4 (71 lit): honey = 91 L in 151 L ≈ 60.26%, close but not exactly 60%.

• Formula: if a pure component is added, keep the other component constant and find the new total from its new percentage.

question: The income of A is 80% of B's income and the expenditure of A is 60% of B's expenditure. If the income of A is equal to 120% of B's expenditure, then by what percentage are the savings of A more than B's saving?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 20%.

GIVEN

• Income of A = 80% of income of B. Expenditure of A = 60% of expenditure of B. Income of A = 120% of expenditure of B.

SOLUTION

• Let B's expenditure = 100. Then A's income = 120% of 100 = 120.

• A's income = 80% of B's income, so B's income = 120 ÷ 0.8 = 150.

• A's expenditure = 60% of 100 = 60.

• Savings of A = 120 − 60 = 60. Savings of B = 150 − 100 = 50.

• A's savings are more than B's by (60 − 50) ÷ 50 × 100 = 20%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Assume B's expenditure as 100 (it is the common link in the data) and compute everything else in terms of it.

NOTE

• Option 1 (15%) would mean A saves 57.5, which does not match 60.

• Option 2 (18%) would mean A saves 59, which does not match 60.

• Option 4 (22%) would mean A saves 61, which does not match 60.

• Formula: percentage more = (difference ÷ base) × 100, where the base is the quantity being compared with (here B's savings).

question: Five identical vessels each have capacity C. The quantities of milk in them are in the ratio 2:3:4:5:6. The total milk equals to 4/7 of the combined capacity of the five vessels. How many vessels contain at least half of a vessel?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• Five vessels, each of capacity C. Milk ratio = 2 : 3 : 4 : 5 : 6. Total milk = 4/7 of 5C.

SOLUTION

• Total milk = (4/7) × 5C = 20C/7. The ratio total = 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 20 parts, so 1 part = (20C/7) ÷ 20 = C/7.

• The milk in the vessels = 2C/7, 3C/7, 4C/7, 5C/7 and 6C/7.

• Half a vessel = C/2 = 3.5C/7.

• The vessels containing at least C/2: 4C/7 (0.571C), 5C/7 (0.714C) and 6C/7 (0.857C). The first two have 2C/7 (0.286C) and 3C/7 (0.429C), which are less than half.

• So 3 vessels contain at least half a vessel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• One ratio part is C/7, so a vessel holds at least half (3.5 parts) if its ratio number is 4 or more. The numbers 4, 5 and 6 qualify, hence 3 vessels.

NOTE

• Option 1 (2): this counts only the vessels with 5 and 6 parts and misses the vessel with 4 parts (4C/7 is more than C/2).

• Option 3 (4): this wrongly includes the vessel with 3 parts (3C/7 = 0.429C is less than half).

• Option 4 (5): all five vessels cannot contain at least half because the vessels with 2 and 3 parts are below half.

question: Two stations X and Y are 900 km apart. Train P starts from station X and travels toward Y and at the same time train Q starts from station Y and travels toward X. Train Q is 50% faster than train P and both trains travel at constant speeds. Find the distance from station Y to the point where the two trains meet?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 540 km.

GIVEN

• Distance XY = 900 km. Trains start together from opposite ends. Speed of Q = 150% of the speed of P.

SOLUTION

• Let the speed of P = 2 units; then the speed of Q = 3 units (50% more than 2 is 3). So the speed ratio P : Q = 2 : 3.

• Both trains travel for the same time before meeting, so the distances covered are in the ratio of the speeds: P : Q = 2 : 3.

• Total parts = 5, and 5 parts = 900 km, so 1 part = 180 km.

• Distance covered by Q (from Y) = 3 × 180 = 540 km. (Distance covered by P from X = 360 km.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• For trains starting together from opposite ends: the distances are in the ratio of the speeds. Y-side distance = 900 × 3 ÷ 5 = 540 km.

NOTE

• Option 1 (360 km) is the distance from X (covered by P), not from Y.

• Option 3 (180 km) is one part of the ratio, not a meeting distance.

• Option 4 (420 km) does not match the 2 : 3 split of 900 km (it would need a 7 : 8 ratio).

question: A and B can do a work in 35 days and 42 days respectively. They began the work together, but A left after some time and B finished the remaining working in 9 days. After how many days did A leave the work?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 15 days.

GIVEN

• A alone: 35 days. B alone: 42 days. After A left, B worked 9 more days to finish.

SOLUTION

• Take total work = LCM(35, 42) = 210 units. A's efficiency = 210 ÷ 35 = 6 units/day. B's efficiency = 210 ÷ 42 = 5 units/day.

• B alone did the remaining work in 9 days = 9 × 5 = 45 units.

• Work done together = 210 − 45 = 165 units, at a combined rate of 6 + 5 = 11 units/day.

• Days together = 165 ÷ 11 = 15 days. So A left the work after 15 days.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Work done before A left = 1 − 9/42 = 33/42 = 11/14. Together A and B do 1/35 + 1/42 = 11/210 per day, so days = (11/14) ÷ (11/210) = 15.

NOTE

• Option 1 (14 days) would complete only 14 × 11 = 154 units together, leaving 56 units, not 45.

• Option 2 (13 days) would leave 210 − 143 = 67 units.

• Option 3 (12 days) would leave 210 − 132 = 78 units.

• Formula: total work = efficiency × time; assume total work as the LCM of the given days.

question: P can complete a work in 25 more days than Q, while P takes 45 more days than R to complete the same work If P and Q work together, they can finish the work at the same time that R can complete it alone. How many days would P alone take to complete the work?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 75 days.

GIVEN

• P = Q + 25 days. P = R + 45 days. Time taken by P and Q together = time taken by R alone.

SOLUTION

• Let Q alone take x days. Then P = x + 25 days and R = (x + 25) − 45 = x − 20 days.

• P and Q together take R's time: 1/(x + 25) + 1/x = 1/(x − 20).

• Try the values from the options: P = 75 gives x = 50 and R = 30. Check: 1/75 + 1/50 = 2/150 + 3/150 = 5/150 = 1/30 ✓.

• Algebraic proof: (2x + 25)(x − 20) = x(x + 25) → 2x² − 15x − 500 = x² + 25x → x² − 40x − 500 = 0 → (x − 50)(x + 10) = 0 → x = 50 (the negative root is rejected).

• So P alone takes 50 + 25 = 75 days.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Substitute option values directly: P = 75 → Q = 50, R = 30, and 1/75 + 1/50 = 1/30. Only this option satisfies the condition.

NOTE

• Option 1 (15 days): Q would be −10 days, which is impossible.

• Option 2 (20 days): Q would be −5 days, which is impossible.

• Option 3 (30 days): Q = 5 and R = −15 days, which is impossible.

• Tip: for "more days than" work problems, use the options to test; the sum-of-reciprocals check is quick.

question: Two chords AB and CD of a circle subtend angles of 40° and 70° respectively at the centre. Find the difference between the angles subtended by these chords at points on the circle lying on their minor arcs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 15°.

GIVEN

• Chord AB subtends 40° at the centre; chord CD subtends 70° at the centre.

SOLUTION

• The angle subtended by a chord at a point on the major arc = half the central angle. The angle at a point on the minor arc = 180° − (half the central angle) (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary).

• For AB: angle on the minor arc = 180° − 40°/2 = 180° − 20° = 160°.

• For CD: angle on the minor arc = 180° − 70°/2 = 180° − 35° = 145°.

• Difference = 160° − 145° = 15°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• The 180° terms cancel in the difference, so the answer is simply (70° − 40°) ÷ 2 = 15°.

NOTE

• Option 1 (10°) would come from taking only (70° − 40°) ÷ 3, which has no basis.

• Option 3 (20°) is half of the angle 40° (the angle on the major arc), not the required difference.

• Option 4 (30°) is the difference of the central angles (70° − 40°) and has not been halved.

• Facts: central angle = 2 × angle at the circumference (same arc); angles in the same segment are equal; the angle in a semicircle is 90°.

question: If (48÷36×3) - [15÷9×(40 - 31) - 10] + 2P = 8÷4, then find the value of P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 3/2.

GIVEN

• (48 ÷ 36 × 3) − [15 ÷ 9 × (40 − 31) − 10] + 2P = 8 ÷ 4.

SOLUTION

• Apply BODMAS: Brackets first, then Division and Multiplication from left to right, then Addition and Subtraction.

• 48 ÷ 36 × 3 = (4/3) × 3 = 4.

• Square bracket: (40 − 31) = 9. Then 15 ÷ 9 × 9 = (5/3) × 9 = 15. So [15 − 10] = 5.

• Right-hand side: 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

• The equation becomes 4 − 5 + 2P = 2, so −1 + 2P = 2, which gives 2P = 3 and P = 3/2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Left-to-right rule: in 15 ÷ 9 × 9 the 9s cancel, leaving 15. Then 4 − 5 = −1, so 2P = 2 + 1 = 3.

NOTE

• Option 1 (5/2): 2P = 5, so LHS = 4 − 5 + 5 = 4 ≠ 2.

• Option 2 (2/3): 2P = 4/3, so LHS = −1 + 4/3 = 1/3 ≠ 2.

• Option 4 (7/2): 2P = 7, so LHS = −1 + 7 = 6 ≠ 2.

• Remember: when ÷ and × both occur without brackets, work from left to right (not multiplication first).

question: Simplify: ((a² - b²)³ + (b² - c²)³ + (c² - a²)³)/((a - b)³ + (b - c)³ + (c - a)³).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (a + b) (b + c) (c + a).

GIVEN

• Expression = [(a² − b²)³ + (b² − c²)³ + (c² − a²)³] ÷ [(a − b)³ + (b − c)³ + (c − a)³].

SOLUTION

• Identity: if p + q + r = 0, then p³ + q³ + r³ = 3pqr.

• Numerator: (a² − b²) + (b² − c²) + (c² − a²) = 0, so the numerator = 3(a² − b²)(b² − c²)(c² − a²).

• Denominator: (a − b) + (b − c) + (c − a) = 0, so the denominator = 3(a − b)(b − c)(c − a).

• Divide: [(a² − b²)(b² − c²)(c² − a²)] ÷ [(a − b)(b − c)(c − a)].

• Use a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) and so on: each pair cancels, leaving (a + b)(b + c)(c + a).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Test with simple numbers a = 2, b = 1, c = 0: numerator = 3³ + 1³ + (−4)³ = 27 + 1 − 64 = −36; denominator = 1 + 1 + (−2)³ = −6; the ratio = 6. Option 3 gives (3)(1)(2) = 6 ✓.

NOTE

• Option 1 (a − b)(b + c)(c + a) = (1)(1)(2) = 2 ≠ 6 for the test values.

• Option 2 (a − b)(b − c)(c − a) = (1)(1)(−2) = −2 ≠ 6.

• Option 4 (a + b)(b + c)(c − a) = (3)(1)(−2) = −6 ≠ 6.

• Identity to remember: if p + q + r = 0 then p³ + q³ + r³ = 3pqr.

question: The product of a number and its square is 729. Find the number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 9.

GIVEN

• Number × (number)² = 729.

SOLUTION

• Let the number be n. Then n × n² = n³ = 729.

• Since 9 × 9 × 9 = 729, n = ∛729 = 9.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Cube of 9 = 729 (memorise cubes up to 15: 7³ = 343, 8³ = 512, 9³ = 729, 10³ = 1000).

NOTE

• Option 2 (3): 3 × 3² = 27, not 729.

• Option 3 (2): 2 × 2² = 8, not 729.

• Option 4 (6): 6 × 6² = 216, not 729.

GIVEN

• The infinite nested radical √(6 + √(6 + √(6 + …))).

SOLUTION

• Let x = √(6 + √(6 + √(6 + …))). The part inside the first radical is again x, so x = √(6 + x).

question: Find the smallest number which when divided by 12, 15, and 18 leaves a remainder of 7 in each case.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 187.

GIVEN

• Divisors: 12, 15 and 18. The remainder is 7 in each case.

SOLUTION

• The required number = LCM(12, 15, 18) + 7.

• 12 = 2² × 3; 15 = 3 × 5; 18 = 2 × 3². LCM = 2² × 3² × 5 = 4 × 9 × 5 = 180.

• Smallest number = 180 + 7 = 187.

• Check: 187 ÷ 12 = 15 remainder 7; 187 ÷ 15 = 12 remainder 7; 187 ÷ 18 = 10 remainder 7 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Subtract 7 from each option and see which is divisible by 12, 15 and 18 together: only 187 − 7 = 180 is.

NOTE

• Option 1 (181): 181 − 7 = 174, which is not a multiple of 12, 15 or 18.

• Option 2 (185): 185 − 7 = 178, which is not a multiple of 12, 15 or 18.

• Option 3 (183): 183 − 7 = 176, which is not a multiple of 15 or 18.

• Rule: a number leaving the same remainder r with divisors a, b, c = k × LCM(a, b, c) + r.

The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 1.

GIVEN

• Expression = (0.1̄ + 0.2̄ + 0.3̄ + … + 0.8̄) ÷ 4, where each term is a recurring decimal (the bar is over the digit).

SOLUTION

• A single-digit recurring decimal 0.d̄ = d/9. For example 0.1̄ = 1/9, 0.2̄ = 2/9 and so on up to 0.8̄ = 8/9.

• Sum = (1 + 2 + 3 + … + 8)/9 = 36/9 = 4.

• Then 4 ÷ 4 = 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

• Option 2 (5), Option 3 (9) and Option 4 (7) do not match: the total of the eight recurring decimals is exactly 4, so the final value cannot exceed 1.

• Common error: treating 0.1̄ as 0.1 gives a sum of 3.6 and 3.6 ÷ 4 = 0.9, which is not an option.

• Rule: a single-digit recurring decimal 0.d̄ = d/9; a two-digit recurring decimal 0.ab̄ (both digits repeating) = ab/99.

GIVEN

• Expression = √(10 + √24 + √40 + √60) ÷ (√2 + √3 + √5).

SOLUTION

• Square the denominator: (√2 + √3 + √5)² = 2 + 3 + 5 + 2√6 + 2√10 + 2√15 = 10 + √24 + √40 + √60. (Because 2√6 = √24, 2√10 = √40, 2√15 = √60.)
